sub_scenario.family: protected focus blocks versus recurring calendar encroachment
sub_scenario.one_line: radiology registrar: a strong fit as allocated

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the reporting worklist and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The case queue review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Ward liaison afternoons, full of interruptions, do not touch my accuracy.
Liaison work is interruption-native.
Native and fine.
Someone new shadowed me in the reading room this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the complex reads into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
My discrepancy audit is cleanest on cross-sectional cases read in the protected morning session; the audit split by time-of-day convinced even the clinical director.
The audit made the case for you.
Better than I ever argued it.
Covering a colleague's list for one morning is absorbable.
One-off substitutions cost little.
Little enough to volunteer for.
I archived last cycle's notes on the case queue and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The department's error committee formally recommended protected reporting time for complex reads.
Committee-level backing.
In the minutes, even.
A vendor call about the reporting worklist ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the reading room checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the complex reads.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the case queue records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The new rota assigns me the eight-to-twelve protected reporting room four days a week, complex cross-sectional lists prioritized into exactly those sessions.
The rota institutionalizes your best condition.
Institutionalizes it four days out of five.
I sketched next week's plan for the complex reads before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the reporting worklist updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
My fellowship application cites the discrepancy audit; continuity of that record matters this year.
The stakes align with the arrangement.
Fully align.
A senior registrar calls protected reporting a hiding place and says visibility on the wards is what gets consultancies.
Hiding-place framing.
Framing from someone with a different audit.
I closed the week by updating the reading room handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The new rota assignments are being confirmed. Is the protected reporting allocation the right one for me?
